# Chapter 32 of the First Book
<header>Concerning the Distress of Water.</header>

...the state of fire and water is not fixed; for they move through them. Their outlets are visible, but their true positions lie beneath; and though they are invisible, they are roughly known because one can drive through to them. One sees how water sweats out of the marble, or how the air brings it in—or becomes water itself. So too, one sees how the **vapors** <note>original: *Witterung*; in this context, the internal atmosphere or "weather" within the earth that was believed to generate minerals</note> in the hard stones become fire, for it is struck out from them. From this arise the **burning blights** <term>uredines</term> <note>original: *uredines*; a Latin term used here to describe a transformative subterranean heat or "burning" that acts upon the earth to generate metals</note> which, through their power, create the metals out of the earth-stuff <note>the raw mineral matrix or material of the earth</note>. Where so much of this earth-stuff has been consumed that holes are formed, the water soon fills them up—just as the fire is soon there again and fills the "bung-hole" of the water. Thus, stone is in eternal change, just like all other things.

Such holes, or swamps and "galls" <note>referring to pockets of liquid or impurities in the rock</note>, are the **Distress of Water**. If **surface water** <term>Tagwaſſer</term> <note>water from rain or snowmelt entering from above</note> is added to this, the damage is even greater. This surface water is of no use at all to the **ground water** <term>Grund-Waſſer</term>, for it displaces it significantly and makes it poisonous. 

In **Hungary**, there is not such great distress, for there is not so much surface water there because the soil is full of lime. But the others in **Bohemia** and **Meissen** suffer very great hindrances. # The First Book, Chapter 34.

People, although they do not know where **fluxes** <note>original: *Flüsse*; likely referring to fluorite or similar glass-like minerals that assist in melting</note> come from, can make nothing of them. They are indeed fluid when they are put into the fire, but one can introduce nothing into them, for they allow no air into themselves, nor any of the qualities in the air that might make them more noble. For it is a strange thing in nature: when something good is driven out of a **body** <note>original Latin: *corpore*</note>, especially by force, it will not go back in. For when life is taken from a person, it cannot be given back to him; the **body** <note>German: *Cörper*</note> accepts it no more, even if he died naturally—though for God, it is indeed possible. 

But I am not writing here of miracles, but of what is natural and based on experience; I rightly leave the other matters aside. And it is very strange that the **body** <note>original Latin: *corpus*</note> of deceased metals is so beautiful, whereas other **bodies** <note>original Latin: *corpora*</note> decay and come to nothing—though eventually, over a long time, that happens to the metal as well. # Book 1, Chapter 35

...the stone is that very same meal. Thus, the marrow <note>original: *Marck*; referring to a soft, fatty, or pithy mineral substance found inside rocks</note> is the softest part of all and clings very readily to the quartz <term>Kißling</term> <note>a historical term for pebbles, quartz, or flinty river stones</note>, for it originates from them. For when a fire or vapor reaches a quartz stone and burns it, the exterior—the shell—becomes such meal. The water, however, enters inside—especially if it was somewhat hollow within—and draws the interior into itself to become marrow. This is especially caused by the extreme cold fire; for heat and cold must perform their work down below, where they are not as tempered as they are up here on the surface. Wherever they strike and cast their rays, such meal and marrow are formed by that same heat and subterranean cold.

Just as the sun, where it shines and casts its rays, performs its own work—which I call the upper burns <term>Uredines</term> <note>original: *Uredines*; a Latin term for blights or scorching winds. The author is comparing solar radiation to subterranean mineral "rays"</note>. These rays, however, have their subterranean source in the metals—the cold rays from cold metals, the hot rays from hot ones. If they should strike someone, let him beware! Just as they cause damage to the young fruits of the earth, they also harm the stones, waters, and air. 

If someone should fall into such misfortune beneath the earth and receive a "blast" <note>original: *Schuß*; likely referring to a sudden discharge of gas or a rock burst caused by internal pressure</note>, let him accept it as best he can and see how he may be rid of its effects; it is better that he stay out of the way and let the stone "shoot" so that it may turn to meal and marrow. 

Such meal, however, clogs the pores <note>original: *Poros*; the tiny openings or passages within the rock strata</note> and creates a stagnation of air <term>Wettersatz</term> <note>a traditional mining term for foul, stagnant, or unbreathable air that fails to circulate</note> so that the fresh air cannot follow after. For even the fire cannot lift it, and it thereafter consumes the stone continuously. Thus, the stone-marrow works from the inside out until they finally come together and form such a strange potter’s meal <note>original: *Töpener Mehl*; likely a reference to a fine, clay-like mineral dust used in ceramics</note>. ## On the Self-Blower.

The "Self-Blower" is an instrument that corrects the "foul weather" <note>original: *böses Wetter*; a mining term for dangerous or stagnant gases in a mine shaft</note> or the displaced air. For displaced air does not create stone—otherwise everything containing it would turn to stone—rather, stone forms where the internal fire draws in [substance] instead of air and dries it, though without igniting it. This is clearly seen when one strikes off a fragment <note>original: *Haucke*; a chip or flake of rock</note> with a pick; one sees how it leaps out. This leaping fragment allows us to understand how Nature creates stone, and likewise how it creates ore or metal, for they are essentially the same thing. Only noble gemstones have a different origin, arising from "sweet waters" <note>fresh water, as opposed to mineralized or salt water</note>.

Now, in such an instrument, fire and air are brought together; it draws its power and material from the "foul weather." The fire consumes whatever "heavy" elements are within that air and lightens <note>original: *erleuchtet*; likely meaning to make less dense or to purify the air</note> the remaining part which it carries. This blower is constructed as a sphere made of copper, about the size of a head. It is entirely hollow and soldered tightly so that no air may enter, except through a tiny hole—no larger than what a needle might fit into—and it sucks...

For these fissures are indeed the pipes and channels that carry the sub-terrestrial water; even if they occasionally contain ore, the value of that ore is often consumed by the expenses one spends before one can remove the water that is unleashed.

# CHAPTER XLV.
## OF THE GLOWING FIRE,

<image-desc>Faint ink sketch in the left margin next to the chapter heading, resembling a long, narrow triangular object or a stylus.</image-desc>

This fire is directed at the **metallic bodies** <note>original: *corpora metallorum*</note>, which it consumes through the materials they naturally possess that are prone to it. For this reason, I must hold this fire in high regard; the bodies that remain become quite malleable, while the **waste products** <note>original: *exuvia*, literally "cast-off skins," referring here to the impurities or dross separated from the metal</note> are left behind on the spot. The very best thing about them is that through the glowing heat, they cast off everything that ought to be removed, while the other part remains.

It would be even better, however, if one first placed the material into a **washing works** <term>washing works: a facility (Waschwerk) where ore was crushed and washed with water to separate heavy metallic particles from lighter waste rock before the smelting process began</term>, so that the water might remove whatever it can with less damage before one hurries to the fire with it. For be that as it may, once the fire is applied, it attacks. I cannot find fault with the roasting process, but when something is lost during the roasting that should have remained, that is too much and it "robs" the metal. The scent reveals this: if a roasting smells more like raw minerals than like metal, then the metal is already partially destroyed.

For look at **iron**: it gives off its **dross** <note>original: *Exuvium*</note>, and **copper** also yields its **sinter** <term>sinter: the scale or oxidation crust that forms on the surface of heated metal</term> or **slag**. However, if it flares up violently, it robs and consumes the iron. For this reason, **pit-coal** <note>original: *SteinKohlen*</note>—which contains so much **sulfur**—is not good for iron; it burns the iron and carries it away so that nothing but idle sinter remains, which is a pity. I hold it as most certain that one should not [use] one of these things alone...

### Chapter 45 of the First Book

The second kind of **roasting** involves a great loss of metals and the expense of the vessels, especially if you roast in a **robbing-furnace** <note>original: *Räuber*; a type of furnace or crucible known for "stealing" or absorbing the metal being processed</note>, or in glass or other clay vessels. Although these may be reinforced with iron or copper plates, when the great heat arrives, they become prone to melting and are thus not suitable for the metal. Clay, glass, and slag are not metals; therefore, the metal suffers a decrease within them and cannot be properly mastered. For this reason, look closely at what kind of metal you wish to treat, so that you may provide it with the rightful fire. This is indeed the very best fire for metals and for their **transmutation** <note>the alchemical process of changing one substance into another, such as lead into gold</note>. For you can see it even in the hardest metals, which cast off their **bodies** <note>original: *corpora*</note> during the roasting. For tell me, what is the **body** of iron or copper other than its slag? Its **soul** <note>original: *Anima*</note> or its **tincture** <note>the concentrated spiritual essence or coloring principle of a metal</note> departs, as you can clearly see in the smelting; when you throw them into the glowing heat, they fly away in a flame. Therefore, one must have them "doubled" <note>likely referring to the reinforcement or capture of these volatile spirits</note> so that they serve the metal and allow it to be worked correctly.

Otherwise, roasting is also useful for the **bodies of stones**, as it turns them into **lime** <note>original: *calce*</note>. Therefore, neither they nor anyone else should wonder why they have accomplished or achieved nothing good. For let everyone think rightly for themselves what the **calcination** <note>the process of heating a substance to high temperatures to change its physical or chemical state</note> in a **reverberatory furnace** <note>original: *reverber*; an open-fire furnace where the flame is "thrown back" onto the material</note>—that same harsh roasting—is supposed to do or preserve when the vessels (even the earthen ones) are not **sealed with lute** <note>original: *verlutiret*; sealed with a specialized alchemical clay or cement to make them airtight</note>, and the **Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurius*; here referring to the volatile "spirit" or quicksilver essence of the metal</note>...

### CHAPTER XLVI.

## CONCERNING THE CORROSIVE FIRE,
or
## Of the Corrosive Fire. <insert>consuming</insert> <insert>devouring</insert>

This fire must be categorized among the cold fires, for they consume. This consumption occurs within the cold fire, for it possesses the same nature as burning fire—it shines and burns. Its burning, however, is corrosion <note>original: *Etzen*</note>. In this, it is better than other fires, for it does not burn entirely to ash, but rather reduces the body <note>original: *corpus*</note> completely into a fine ore-powder <term>Schlich: Usually refers to washed ore-slime or fine powder, suggesting the acid has disintegrated the solid metal</term>. This is something that could otherwise not be achieved even with great effort, even if one were to file the metal into shavings. For it dissolves the bonds of the atoms from which it is composed. For there are atoms beneath the earth just as there are above, which the atmosphere <note>original: *Witterung*; can refer to air, weather, or the "spirit of the air" in alchemy</note> leads to the body, strengthening and increasing it. Only this fire pulls such things apart. # CHAPTER XLIX.

## Of the Warm Fire.

Now this warm fire, just as the cold fire is the cause of the skin forming from the seed, so this fire tears that skin apart. Although it does not do so in a single way or at a single time, it nevertheless takes its own time and labor for the task. Therefore, learn to properly consider the nature of each fire. The application of this fire is manifold, of which you have previously heard enough regarding how it should be managed—whether in coals, in wood, in pitch, oil, and in summary, in everything that can be burned here above. This is what I mean now, although I speak here only of the warmth that is useful to the metals for their **flow** <note>original: *fluß*; the molten state of metal necessary for its transformation</note>, for in that state they purify themselves, as you have heard above.

Thus—and this is well worth noting—no heat or fire is good for the metals if it touches the work with its direct strength. Rather, it must occur in a <term>double vessel: *duplici vasculo*; an alchemical setup where the primary container is placed inside a second one (like a water or sand bath) to prevent direct contact with the flame</term>, which I call a double vessel; there, the fire cannot touch the **body** <note>original: *corpus*; the physical substance of the metal</note>, but instead the fire strengthens the heat. ...the warmth. For a harsh heat is not good—that is, where the naked fire touches a thing closely, it burns, just as the sun does when it is at its highest fervor. Instead, it is good where it warms—that is, where something lies in between, such as water, so that I may enjoy the heat of the fire and the water together: warmth. 

In the same way, warmth occurs when I have the metal in a vessel, so that only the heat of that same vessel communicates the warmth to the metal. Now, the warmth of glass or clay does this well, but it is harmful; for it is not full, but empty of such a substance that should be serviceable to the metal and also strengthen it—not the harsh heat, but the gentle warmth. 

Therefore one sees, as I have often said regarding the vessels of the alchemists, that they do not truly consider the **matter** <note>original: *materia*; here meaning the physical material the vessel is made of</note> of the equipment, but only the forms—how many **beaks and bellies** <note>refers to the various spouts (*Schnäbel*) and rounded glass bodies (*Bäuche*) of alchemical stills like alembics and retorts</note> they should have. They do not consider how they might dampen the heat and provide varied warmth. Because of this, they achieve little. They may serve in part to extract the <term>spirit: *spiritum*; the volatile, vaporous essence of a substance</term> and the <term>quintessence: *quintam essentiam*; the "fifth element" or the most purified, medicinal core of a material</term>, but that is not true metallic work; it is too weak for that purpose. 

The **forge-fires** <note>original: *Eßfeuer*; referring to the hearth or forge furnace used in blacksmithing and smelting</note> are more beneficial to the ore or the metals, for they attack the metals within the ore and leave the rest to the fire, because they also possess a hidden warmth, rather than a harsh heat that causes damage. For a naked heat only brings about damage and mischief. In the art of distilling, people have now come somewhat closer to the truth, where they have dampened the heat with sand, ash, **iron scale** <note>original: *Hammerschlag*; the oxide flakes that fall from hot iron when struck on an anvil; used here as a medium for a dry heat bath</note>, and so on, and the warm-

# Of the Warm Fire.

[...has] strengthened me; but people have not been able to consider this enough regarding metal: that it was more necessary there—particularly to dampen its heat and strengthen the warmth with a **body** <note>original: *corpore*; the physical substance or "matrix" that holds the spirit</note>, so that it would have been satisfied. This is especially true for the seed or the **Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurius*; in alchemy, the volatile, transformative principle</note>. For as soon as the heat seizes the **Mercury**, it does not remain; it does not turn into the flow or into the **slickness** <note>original: *lubricum*; an oily, fluid state</note>, and thus into a **body**, but rather into the **volatile** <note>original: *volatile*; the state of evaporating or turning into vapor</note>. There it perishes like a **body** when the heat seizes its raw flesh. 

This warm fire is also necessary so that warmth may be understood more than heat—especially the "free fire" that strikes against a thing, or into which it is thrown, or under which it is placed. In between these, it must be so distressed <note>original: *geängstiget*; a term for applying pressure or intense heat to force a transformation</note> that not much of it remains; for that is what heat does when it gains the upper hand. 

The smelters understood this well, too, having introduced the process of **fining** <note>original: *Erfrischen*; a metallurgical term for purifying metal (often iron or silver) by removing carbon or lead</note> so that it does not entirely sink to the bottom and perish. Thus, this fire is directed more at the **body** <note>original: *corpus*</note> than at everything alongside the body—such as the fats, litharge <note>original: *Gläten*; lead oxide produced during the separation of silver</note>, and slag <note>original: *Floß*</note>. For these do not belong in this fire; the fire attacks them, but those same accompanying impurities then attack the **body** as well through the heat, driving away the seed and the **vital spirit** <note>original: *Ferch*; an archaic term for the "life-blood" or essential vitality of a substance</note> within it, and thus the spirit passes away with them. 

For you must not understand the **body** <note>original: *corpus*</note> as if it has its own nature alone, and the seed likewise; rather, always remember in every work you undertake that if you do too much to one, you do it to all, if you do not pay such heed to it—

<header>Of the Instruction of the Mountains /</header>

[informed by] a magnet of the compass where **East**, **West**, **South**, or **North** <note>original: *Morgen, Abend, Mittag, oder Mitternacht*—early German mining terminology often used times of day to indicate the four cardinal directions</note> may be; as well as truly to fathom this or that rock in its **strikes** <term>strike: the horizontal direction or compass bearing of a geological feature, such as an ore vein</term>, also to have and hold them together with their emergence, for good instruction, regarding both the long and short mountain ranges, how they extend at the top for the longest time in a uniform shape. The forms of such mountain ranges are varied: Firstly, one part contains many glistening, talc-bearing shales, such as **silver- and lead-mountains**; another part is in a coarse rock, in which there is little shale and talc—these are to be recognized by their hardness; another part are rocks in which copper and **tin-flowers** <note>original: *Zwitter-Blumen*; "Zwitter" was a common term for tin-ore among miners, and "flowers" refers to the crystalline or bloom-like appearance of the mineral</note> shine forth; and in part also flat **seams** <term>seam (Flöz): a layer or bed of ore-bearing rock</term> and shale-rock, in which copper ore is also formed. Therefore, it is well to be gathered from Nature that because of various forms, various **fruits** <note>the "fruits" of the earth refer to the ores and minerals produced by natural processes</note> are also attained; there, one finds in the **Southern mountains**, which are better than those parts toward the **West**, which are called the **secondary mountains** or ends, between which a center of perfection is always ordered.

## CHAPTER IV.

# Of Silver Ore, its Rock Formation, Action, Nature, and Striking Veins.

<margin>A</margin>Silver ore is also formed in its own stone, arising from a quite perfect nature and a beautiful, noble earth, and from the most stable, clear **sulfur**, its **salt**, and **mercury** <note>original symbols: Sulphur, Salt, and ☿. These are the "Tria Prima" or three primary substances of alchemy believed to constitute all matter</note>, which join together in a mixture with a powerful bond. This occurs in such a way that it appears to be of a lower degree than **gold** <note>original symbol: ☉, the Sun</note>, and yet, after gold, it is the very best and most stable metal among all those that follow. It suffers very little loss when exposed to fire <note>original: *Verbrennligkeit*; referring to the fact that silver, like gold, does not oxidize or "burn away" easily during smelting</note> and can be brought out of the fire and separated by itself or from other **metals**. That which its naturally well-disposed stone—the natural silver **rock formation** <term>Gebürge; in early mining, this referred both to the mountain and the specific geological host rock</term>—causes, nevertheless follows the heavenly influence and the night-light of the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note>. For this reason, the most **silver veins** are found in the northern <note>original: *mitnächtigen*; literally "midnight," a traditional term for the North</note> lands. For just as the Moon has the Sun to its right and receives its light from it, so and in like manner the silver veins and silver stone have the gold veins to their right. <margin>A</margin>Thus, a "root" is compared to the noble **Lunar Queen** <note>original: *Lunariæ*; the feminine personification of silver in alchemy</note>, from which the **gold vein** receives all the more strength and power in its mixture; the mountains themselves attain these qualities from their roots. # On Lead Ore
CA.

...[of God] the mountains of metals; if only mankind used them correctly, then everything would be without lack, and a good supply would be at hand; but where one uses such things ignorantly, one has little profit from them. For just as a chain is made from its <term>soul <note>original: Seele; in early modern mining and alchemy, this refers to the essential spiritual or chemical principle that gives a metal its properties.</note></term>, which draws and joins together the joints and gold-fissures, as well as silver, so it also possesses a particular spirit that can be distilled into a water through the visible and invisible <term>alembic <note>original: Helm; literally the "helmet" or cap of a distillation apparatus; here used metaphorically to describe how vapors in the earth condense into minerals.</note></term>. Just as nature in the earth turns such waters into ice upon its veins, hardening them into a signpost and certain mark by which everyone recognizes that it is a <term>lead-streak <note>original: Bleyschweiff; literally "lead-tail," referring to a fine-grained, shimmering variety of galena that often appears as a thin streak, indicating a larger vein is nearby.</note></term> and a sure indication of its own lead vein—whether it has other metallic deposits or not, it is all the more pleasant and better for it.

The best lead veins, however, and the most consistent among all of them, are the water-blue, scaly, talc-like <term>shale rocks</term>, gritty and with elongated <term>fluor-quartz <note>original: Fluß-Quark; a historical term combining "Fluß" (fluorite) and "Quark" (an old mining term for quartz or base rock).</note></term>, or sprinkled in circles and not twisted, but rather coarsely fissured, with horizontal veins and uniform structures, in some parts not unlike the silver mountains. Some lead mountains are also made of a white-scaly talc-shale full of "wild" <term>garnets</term>, or undulating here and there, in which silver-rich lead ores show themselves.

## CHAPTER VIII.

# On Tin / its Mountains / Workings / Mists / Stocks / Seams / Drops and Striking Veins.

Tin ore is formed within a sandstone, in accordance with the celestial influence of **Jupiter** <note>original: Jovis; in alchemy and early natural philosophy, tin was the metal cosmologically linked to the planet Jupiter.</note>. It appears dark-black and brown, purple-colored, greyish, or black-shining, and is composed of a mercury, salt, and a small amount of mixed sulfur. With these are mingled unpleasant, coarse, sulfurous **vapors** <note>original: Bradem; an archaic term for the exhalations or fumes within the earth believed to condense into minerals.</note> which embody and bind together to create the metal tin. It is because of these unpleasant vapors that every kind of tin becomes "crunchy" <note>This refers to the "cry of tin," a characteristic crackling sound made when bending a bar of the metal.</note> and brittle, so much so that it also makes all other metals melted with it unpleasant and brittle.

Such tin, or **tin-ore** <term>Zwitter <note>original: Zwitter; a specific historical term in Saxon mining for tin-bearing rock or cassiterite, often found in granitic formations.</note></term>, occurs in three types and colors: namely, in veins, in mists, or in "stocks" <note>Massive, irregular ore bodies as opposed to thin veins.</note>. It also contains three kinds of **impurities** <term>Wildnuß <note>original: Wildnuß; literally "wildness," referring to the non-valuable minerals or gangue rock that grow alongside the ore.</note></term>, such as **crusts** <note>original: Schöll; likely referring to rocky shells or shaly inclusions.</note>, **pyrite** <note>original: Kiß; historical spelling of Kies, usually referring to iron pyrites.</note>, and **iron-stain** <note>original: Eisenmahl; iron-bearing minerals that color the ore.</note>, from which it yields "hard work" <note>Refers to ore that is difficult to smelt or process due to these contaminants.</note>. Its colors are primarily black, slate-brown, and yellow.

Such sandstone and tin-ore mountains contain many mighty, powerful, upright veins and faces within them which reveal themselves at the surface <note>original: am Tag; literally "at the day," a mining term for the surface or outcropping.</note> with tin-ore. Some have very rich "milling-work" <note>Ore suitable for being crushed in a stamp mill.</note>; the pyrite in some must be roasted; and some contains much talc and **mica** <term>KatzenSilber <note>original: KatzenSilber; literally "cat's silver," a mocking name for mica because its metallic shine deceptively resembles silver.</note></term>, which is the "nourishment" of the tin-ore, in which it likes to reside. Other types appear glimmering and iron-stained, and some also strike through **flint-stone** <note>original: Feurgestein; likely referring to quartz or other hard silicate rocks that strike sparks.</note>,

### CHAPTER IX.
# Of Mercury Ore and its Veins.

Mercury ore is produced within its own mountain stones according to its nature, consisting of salt-earths and nimble, volatile earths—of a moist, greasy, slimy, watery oiliness <note>original: Olität; an alchemical term referring to the "oily" or flammable principle thought to exist within minerals.</note>. This is mixed with the most subtle, raw-sulfurous, cooked earth in the weakest, most gradual connection, acting as a premature, pleasant fruit of all particular metals.

<margin>Mercury</margin>
Mercury demonstrates its virtue in many strange ways and shares its active nature and power with minerals and metallic sulfurs, as well as bordering upon **antimonial stones** <term>Spießgläsige Gestein <note>Stibnite or antimony ore, which often resembles glass when processed.</note></term>. It is also readily found where the **tin-mountains** lie higher than the **silver veins**. This requires a much-repeated, powerful action upon other ores, manifesting also in other foreign stones; it is pushed and drawn through the juices <note>original: Safft; the "liquors" or liquid precursors believed to form minerals in the earth.</note> of minerals and metals that are befriended to one another. These produce many strange, miraculous births, making it agreeable to the metals, so that goldsmiths are able to **amalgamate** and gild with it.

It is also made into metallic pigments, prepared into oil and water for health, and **sublimated** <note>The process of vaporizing and re-solidifying a substance to purify it.</note> to become the most terrible poison for etching. It is a true **thief** <note>original: Räuber (robber); refers to mercury’s ability to "steal" or dissolve other metals like gold and silver into itself.</note>, for it gladly takes away and carries with it whatever effort and expense one has spent upon it...

You should know, my friend and lover of wisdom / that in this my undertaken work of manual operations <note>original: "Handgriffe," referring to practical laboratory techniques</note>, I have not without cause or in vain made the beginning / concerning the two preceding parts on mining matters / minerals and metals / together with their ore / but rather deemed it quite necessary to hold out a clear light and shining lamp to the ignorant / and to make known / that all creations of these same minerals and metals / as well as ore / are formed by a single spirit from above / take their origin in the earth / generate themselves, and come to light / for the earth is at all times ready and eager / to grasp and retain within itself such a spirit / which proceeds from the powers of heaven / until it visibly represents a form and perfection. But how such a thing happens / has already been sufficiently narrated in my previous writings / therefore I repeat it only briefly / in this manner and thus:

Know / that all things come from a heavenly influence and impression / elemental operation and effect / earthly substance and essence / so that from such a mixture, the elements subsequently spring forth / namely water / air, and earth / these then give birth through the help of fire / which lies hidden within them / by means of a warm decoction <note>original: "Kochung," the alchemical process of heating a substance to mature or refine it</note> / a soul, a spirit, and a body / these three are the first <term>Principles <note>original: "Principia," the fundamental components of all matter in the alchemical tradition.</note></term>, which finally, through <term>coagulation <note>The process by which a liquid or spirit becomes a solid or fixed substance.</note></term>, pass into a <term>Mercury <note>original: "Mercurium," representing the spirit or the fluid, volatile principle of matter.</note></term>, into a <term>Sulphur <note>original: "Sulpur," representing the soul or the oily, combustible principle.</note></term>,

...spirit, a wet, volatile, sulfurous soul, and a dry <term>astral salt</term> <note>The "astral" salt refers to the crystalline principle believed to be derived from celestial influences.</note>, which, after its dissolution, must be recognized together with the first two in a watery form. This is particularly to be noted; and I hope you will not take offense at my previous writings, should they seem to be a contradiction to this report and book. 

For although I indicated that the <term>Spirit, Soul, and Body</term> <note>The alchemical trinity: Spirit (Mercury), Soul (Sulfur), and Body (Salt/Earth).</note> come from one metallic essence and must be prepared—among which I named the best, namely Gold—I did so as befits a <term>Philosopher</term> <note>original: "Philosopho"; referring to a practitioner of the "Hermetic Philosophy" or alchemy.</note>, as the ancient sages before me have also done. # The Third Book. #

...[vitrio]lum <note>Completing the word *Vitriolum* (Vitriol) from the previous page.</note> called, for this reason: because its spiritual <margin><image-desc>Pencil mark resembling a trident or alchemical symbol</image-desc></margin> **oil** <note>original: "oleum"</note> contains and encompasses all three **principles** of every victory within itself.

When you have now obtained such a highly refined and well-purified mineral, called **Vitriol**, then pray to GOD for understanding and wisdom for your undertaking, and after its **calcination** <term>Calcination</term> <note>The process of heating a substance to high temperatures in order to drive off volatile parts or reduce it to a powder.</note> place it into a strong, well-coated **retort** <term>Retort</term> <note>A glass flask with a long, curved neck used for distilling chemicals.</note>; drive over or out at first gently, and then more strongly, the snow-white **spirit of Vitriol** in the form of a terrible, monstrous vapor or wind, until it ceases of its own accord. # Manual Procedure

Once the ruby-colored golden water is ready, distill it over so that it is combined; in this way it becomes one, just as it was originally. Preserve it well and diligently so that nothing evaporates, and pour it six times onto beautiful, pure, and refined <term>silver-calx</term> <note>original: "Silber-Kalck." # On the Sulfur of Gold <note>original: "Sulphure Solis." In alchemy, "Sulfur" refers to the combustible, active, or "soul" principle of a metal.</note>

...part **flowers of sulfur** <note>original: "florum sulphuris." A fine powder produced by sublimating natural sulfur.</note>, and let it smoke away again under the **muffle** <note>A clay oven or enclosure used to protect the material from direct flame while allowing high heat.</note>. The powder that remains should be heated to a glow with a stronger fire; then, pour it into the **spirit of wine** <note>original: "spiritum vini." High-proof distilled alcohol.</note>. Perform this labor six times, until finally the gold powder becomes as soft and spongy as hard butter. Dry it gently, for it flows very easily. 

Then, take a coated flask which has a hollow tube or **vent** <note>original: "spiraculum." A breathing hole or small opening in the vessel.</note> at the back; **seal** <note>original: "lutire." To seal the joints of laboratory glassware using a specialized paste or clay called "lute."</note> a helm <note>The top part of a still.</note> onto it and attach a **receiver** <note>original: "recipienten." The vessel that collects the distilled liquid.</note>. Place it empty into a strong **sand bath** <note>original: "Sand-Capellen." A container of sand used to distribute heat evenly to a glass vessel.</note> and give it gentle heat at first, then stronger heat, until the flask in the sand is nearly glowing. Then, take the softened yet well-dried gold powder (otherwise the glass will shatter), warm it slightly, and pour it into the tube at the back. Stop the opening quickly, and nimble red drops will soon enter the helm. Maintain the fire at this degree until nothing more rises and no more drops fall into the **receiver**. 

Note, however, that in the **receiver**, there should be placed **spirit of wine** of the highest and best quality, weighing three times as much as the **gold calx** <note>original: "Gold-Kalck." A metal reduced to a powder through calcination (heating).</note>, into which the drops of gold shall fall.

Then take this **spirit of wine**, into which the golden drops have fallen, and put it into a **Pelican** <note>original: "Pelican." A specialized circulatory vessel with two "arms" that return the condensed vapors to the base, resembling the myth of the pelican feeding its young with its own blood.</note>. **Seal it hermetically** <note>original: "sigillirs hermeticè." To create an airtight seal by melting the glass neck of the vessel shut.</note> and **circulate** <note>original: "circuliers." The process of repeatedly evaporating and condensing a liquid within a closed vessel.</note> it for one month. From this, a blood-red stone will form, which flows in the fire like wax. Crush it small and rub **silver calx** into it. Melt them together in a strong crucible. When it has cooled, pour it into **strong water** <note>original: "aqua fort." Usually *aqua fortis* or nitric acid, used here to dissolve the silver and leave the gold.</note>, and a black powder will fall to the bottom. Melt this powder, and you will find as much good gold as the gold powder and the spirit of wine, together with half—

Take **quicklime** <term>Quicklime (original: "lebendigen Kalck") is calcium oxide, a caustic substance produced by heating limestone. ## On the Particular Operation of Saturn, including the Extraction of its Soul and Salt.

The greater part of the world considers **Saturn** <note>original: "Saturnum." The alchemical name for the metal Lead.</note> or **Lead** to be a lowly and worthless metal, and it is often used for very minor and trivial things; yet, if one truly recognized its inner nature, much more useful and excellent things could be prepared from it. Since I have then intended and resolved, in this my final report and practical manual, to clarify all my previous writings <margin><unclear>To 1</unclear></margin> and to leave them behind as a memorable testament, so that even the simple man, though endowed with little understanding, may recognize what I have written before—and of which I myself shall be a witness after the resurrection of my flesh: that I have told no untruth, but have perhaps done more than was proper, and have explained here and there in my writings all that which others before me kept secret—I have therefore also resolved to explain and report from a true and solid foundation all the **Particulars** <term>Particularia: specific alchemical procedures intended to achieve a particular transmutation or medicinal result, as opposed to the "Universal" work of the Philosopher's Stone.</term> which I have previously mentioned many times in words and outlined in a philosophical manner. I do this in such a way that, in my final years, I wish once again to admonish the one who receives this, my last explanation, by his conscience (as I have before), to pay heed and to observe with diligent <margin>A</margin> care that he [treat] this revelation—which is sent to him in no other way than through the will, counsel, and providence of the Creator of all creatures—in a special manner; the true- <note>original: "das wah-". This is a catchword for "das wahre" (the true) which would begin the following page.</note>

<summary>The author introduces a new section on the alchemical secrets of lead (Saturn), describing it as a misunderstood metal of great potential. Then grind the remaining material small and pour new distilled vinegar upon it, and extract its salt in the warmth. Distill the vinegar away from the salt and remove the acidity by repeated distillation with distilled water; clarify it until the water is found to be beautiful, white, and clear. If you have completed the work correctly through these manual techniques, you will have extracted the salt of Antimony <note>original: "sal Antimonii"</note> in a shorter time, as I shall also mention to you in what follows. In this, you should note that the sulfur of Antimony, prepared and extracted in the following manner, has this same effectiveness <note>original: "efficaciam"</note> in medicine, but it proceeds much faster and more handily, which is particularly to be loved.

Practical Operation

## The short way to make the Sulfur and the Salt of Antimony is as follows.

<margin>Water?</margin>
Take one pound each of good vitriol, common salt, and unslaked lime, and eight **lots** <term>original: "Loht"; a historical German unit of weight, approximately 14-17 grams or half an ounce</term> of sal ammoniac. Crush everything small and put it into a glass flask. Pour three pounds of common wine vinegar over it and let it stand sealed in the warmth for one day. Then put everything together into a **retort** <note>a glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distilling liquids</note>, attach a receiver, and drive it out as one is accustomed to driving out **aqua fortis** <term>literally "strong water"; usually nitric acid, here used as a potent solvent</term>. Take one pound of this distilled liquid <note>original: "liquoris"</note> and one pound of common salt <note>original: "salis communis"</note> and **rectify** <note>to purify a liquid by repeated distillation</note> it once more very slowly, so that nothing cloudy passes over, but everything becomes beautifully clear. Then take one pound of finely powdered **glass of antimony** <term>original: "vitrum antimonii"; a reddish, translucent glass made from roasted antimony ore</term>, pour the spirits over it, **lute** it well <note>seal the vessel's joints with an airtight paste</note>, and digest it until everything is dissolved. Then gently draw off the water in a **Bain-Marie** <term>original: "B. M." or "Balneum Mariae"; a water bath used for gentle, even heating</term>, and a black, thick-fluid matter remains at the bottom, somewhat dry. Lay this upon a glass plate and set it in the cellar.
<margin>X</margin>
In this way, a red oil flows from it, leaving a few dregs <note>original: "feces"</note> behind. Coagulate this red oil very gently on the ashes until it has become dry; then pour the best **spirit of wine** <term>original: "spiritum vini"; concentrated alcohol</term> over it, and the spirit of wine will extract the tincture as blood-red. Pour off the colored liquid and pour more spirit of wine onto the residue until no more redness appears. In this way, you have the **Tincture** or **Sulfur of Antimony**. It works wonders in medicine and (as was also said before in the first process) is not much inferior to **potable gold** <term>original: "auro potabili"; a legendary alchemical medicine thought to grant long life</term>.

## The First Work.

Take of the very best Hungarian gold as much as you wish, and six times as much of good Hungarian antimony <term>antimony: A brittle, silvery-gray metalloid used in alchemy to purify gold</term>, put it into a melting crucible; let it flow well. When it has flowed well, pour it into a casting cone <term>casting cone: A cone-shaped mold used to separate metals of different densities</term> which has been previously warmed and well-greased with wax, as goldsmiths are accustomed to do when they wish to prepare their gold to gild something with it. When it has become cold, remove the antimony from the casting cone; knock the king <term>king: Known as the "regulus" in alchemy, this refers to the refined metallic mass that sinks to the bottom of the mold</term> away from the slag <note>original: "Schlacken" — the stony waste matter separated from metals during smelting</note>; weigh the king, and add to it again six times its weight in new antimony, and do as before: melt it together, pour it out, and knock off the king. Then for the third time add again six parts of antimony and do as before. When this is accomplished, place the <term>Regulus</term> <note>The metallic heart or "king" obtained from the previous steps</note> on a wide cupel <term>cupel: A shallow, porous dish used in refining to separate precious metals from base metals</term> in a furnace, under a muffle <term>muffle: A semi-cylindrical oven insert that protects the material from direct flame while allowing high heat</term>; give it at first a gentle fire, then stronger, until the antimony has evaporated from it and a yellow gold cake remains. Put that into a clean melting crucible before the bellows and blow until the <term>Gold</term> <note>original: "☉" — the alchemical symbol for the Sun and Gold</note> melts well; drive and keep the <term>Gold</term> so long in the fire until the brittleness has entirely evaporated from it, which is to be seen when it allows itself to be worked under the hammer like wax without breaking. # End of the Procedures of Brother Basilius Valentinus regarding the Philosopher's Stone <note>original: Lapidem Philosophorum</note>.

This Universal Work consists of four chapters or operations: The first part of the preparation is the preparation <note>original: præparatio</note> of Gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> with its corresponding solar water; the end of the first part is the purple-colored Gold powder, where the Gold has been well-purged and prepared for further use.

The second part of the preparatory work is the preparation of the Mercury, Sulphur, and Salt of the Philosophers <note>original: ☿, Sulphuris & Salis Philosophorum</note> derived from Antimony <note>symbol: ♁</note> and Iron <note>symbol: ♂</note> until the golden water is thickened; this is the end of the second operation, and herewith the "double mercury" is made.

The third part of the preparatory work is the preparation of the Sulphur of Gold <note>original: Sulphuris Solis</note>, from which the true <term>potable gold</term> <note>original: aurum potabile; a legendary liquid medicine thought to be a universal cure-all made from dissolved gold</note> is to be made; with this, the third operation—and thus the most difficult labor in the Work—is completed.

The fourth part is now the last and final work, acting as the last conjunction and joining together of all things into one, where such things are perfected and carried through to the end.

## Now follows the preparation of the fiery Spirit of Wine.

One should have an instrument made of copper <note>symbol: ♀; associated with the planet Venus</note> / <unclear>d</unclear> in the middle / and the parts below and above the holes <unclear>k</unclear> should be removable / as well as above the half-flask <note>original: Kolben; a glass vessel used in distillation</note>. Upon this, place an alembic <note>original: alembicum; the cap or head of a still</note> with a tube / everything made of glass <note>symbol: ☿; the symbol for Mercury, here referring to the "spirituous" or glass material</note> leading to the receiver / which must be made of glass and be quite large. Place the receiver into a wooden vessel filled with cold water / the receiver must also be covered on top with wet cloths / which are frequently cooled and moistened. In the wooden vessel, there should be a tap / so that one can drain the water / and pour in fresh, cold water again. 

When everything is ready / one pours the prepared spirit of wine <note>original: spiritus vini</note> through the lower holes / filling it just up to the small holes and sets it on fire. Thus the brandy <note>original: Brantwein</note> burns / and the spirit <note>symbol: ☿; the volatile essence</note> is driven upward through the air-holes / and dissolves <note>original: solvirt; here meaning to condense or liquefy</note> because of the cold water / so that it climbs out of the alembic and into the receiver. In this way, the true spirit of wine is prepared. However, you must not fail in the work of cooling at any point / and you must pour in more water of life <note>original: aquam vitæ</note> / so that it does not burn down too low, etc.

# Supernatural, Highly Precious Miracle-Medicine

These then are the foremost ways to make the physical drinkable gold <note>original: *Aurum potabile*</note>; therefore, I will conclude this topic and further demonstrate and describe, with a short yet true process, how silver—which is the next most perfect metal after gold—is also to be made drinkable, and how this drinkable silver <note>original: *argentum potabile*</note> is to be prepared. This process is to be undertaken in the following manner.

<margin>243.</margin>
Take the sky-blue sulfur or spirit of the moon <note>original: *spiritum Lunæ*; in alchemy, the "Moon" represents silver, and its "spirit" is its essential essence</note>, which has been extracted with distilled vinegar, as I have prescribed for you in the specific section on Silver. Wash it until sweet <note>original: *süsse auß*; a process of removing acids or salts by washing with water until the runoff is no longer sharp</note> and rectify it <note>meaning: purify by repeated distillation</note> with spirit of wine <note>original: *spiritu vini*; high-proof alcohol</note>. Let it become dry and place it in a <margin>Nat <unclear>clampig</unclear></margin> vial. Pour over it three times its weight of spirit of mercury <note>original: *spiritus Mercurii*</note>, which is prepared and obtained from the white spirit of vitriol <note>original: *spiritu Vitrioli*; an acidic liquid distilled from sulfate minerals</note>, just as I have most faithfully taught you in that same place. Seal the glass tightly with lute <note>a clay or paste used to hermetically seal laboratory vessels</note> and place it in a vapor bath <note>original: *Balneum vaporosum*; a gentle heating method using steam</note> to putrefy <note>original: *putrificiren*; a stage of alchemical digestion where the substance breaks down and matures</note> for as long as it takes until everything is dissolved <note>original: *solvirt*</note> and nothing more is seen at the bottom. Then add an equal weight of the best spirit of wine; digest them further together for half a month. Finally, distill everything over together <note>original: *treibs alles... herüber*</note> until nothing remains behind. Thus you have the right and true drinkable silver, which performs its work—and can perform it—with wonder in times of need.

Thus now the **coagulated Mercury** <note>original: Mercurius coagulatus</note>, a mineral, must through the Art become water in its **first matter** <note>original: primam materiam</note>—that is, **Mercurial-Water**: That is then a stone / and yet no stone / from which a volatile fire in the **form** of a water is made / which drowns and **dissolves** <note>original: solvirt</note> its fixed father / and its volatile mother.

The **Salt of metals** <note>original: Sal metallorum</note> is an imperfect body <note>original: imperfect Corpus</note> that becomes the **Mercury of the philosophers** <note>original: Mercurius philosophorum</note>, that is, a **permanent or blessed water** <note>original: aqua permanens vel benedicta; a solvent that does not evaporate and is central to the transformation</note> / and is the **Magnet of the Wise** / which loves its **philosophical Mars** <note>The active, "masculine" principle often associated with iron or strength</note> / clings to it and remains with it. Likewise, our gold has a magnet / which magnet is the first root and material of our **Stone**: If you understand this speech of mine / then you are rich before all the world.

**Hermes** <note>referring to Hermes Trismegistus</note> says: You must have three species <note>original: Species; distinct types or substances</note> for the **Work**: Firstly, a **volatile water** <note>original: aquam volatilem</note> or **Mercurial water** / **celestial water** <note>original: aquam coelestem</note>; next, the **Green Lion** <note>original: Leonem viridem; a symbolic term for the raw, acidic mineral or the "life force" of the matter</note>, that is, the **Moon of the philosophers** <note>original: Lunam philosophorum</note>; thirdly, the **Copper of Hermes** <note>original: æs Hermetis</note> or the **Sun** <note>original: Solem</note> or **ferment** <note>original: fermentum</note>.

Finally, note / that the philosophers had two ways: The **wet way** <note>A slower process involving liquid solutions, flasks, and steady heat</note> / which I have used / and then the **dry way** <note>A faster, more intense process using crucibles and high heat</note>: with this you must also act philosophically / so that you purge the **Mercury of the philosophers** well / and make Mercury through Mercury / adding your **philosophical Salt** and **ferment** / or **Sulfur of the philosophers** <note>original: Sulphur philosophorum</note> / and proceed with it / as previously mentioned / so you have the **Magnet of the Wise** / that is, the **Mercury of the philosophers** : thirdly, the **Copper of Hermes** or **Sulfur of the philosophers**.

Thus you have the **Art** entirely / if you do not understand this / then you will have nothing / or shall have nothing from God.

# ALLEGORY
## of the Holy Trinity, and of the Philo-
## sophers’ Stone.

O dear Christian lover of the blessed Art! <note>Alchemy was often called "The Holy Art" by its practitioners</note> How indeed has the Holy Trinity so heartily and wondrously created the *Philosophers’ Stone* <note>original: Lapidem philosophorum</note>? For **GOD** the Father is a Spirit / and yet lets Himself be seen in the form of a man / as He says in His Word in *Genesis chapter 1*: Let us make man / an image / who is like unto us. Likewise / He speaks in His Word and calls His mouth / mouth / eyes / hands and feet. In the same way / the *Mercury of the philosophers* <note>original: Mercurius philosophorum</note> is to be regarded as a *spiritual body* <note>original: spiritualisch corpus; a substance that possesses both physical presence and ethereal properties</note> / as the *philosophers* call it. Out of **GOD** the Father is born His only Son **JESUS Christ** / who is **GOD** and man and is without sin / nor did He need to die: but He died voluntarily and rose again / for the sake of His brothers and sisters / so that they might live with Him eternally without sin. Just so is *Gold* without any defect, and is so fixed <note>In alchemy, "fixed" refers to a substance that is stable and does not evaporate or change when exposed to fire</note> / that it withstands all *tests* <note>original: Examina</note> and heartily / only for the sake of its imperfect and sick brothers and sisters it dies / and rises up gloriously / redeems and tinctures <note>To "tincture" means to transform the very nature of a base metal into a noble one</note> them to eternal life / and makes them *perfect* as good gold.

The third person in the *Trinity* <note>original: Trinitate</note> is **GOD** the Holy Spirit / a Comforter from our **LORD**

## CHAPTER VII.

### Concerning the Sulfur of Antimony. <note>original: De Sulphure Antimonii</note>

->I.<-

One makes a sweet extraction from the Vitriol of Antimony <insert>Vitriol of Antimony</insert> <term>Vitriol of Antimony: A salt-like or glassy substance derived from the mineral stibnite, used as a starting point for many antimony-based medicines.</term> with distilled vinegar, and separates the vinegar <note>original: acetum</note> from it: Upon the residue, one pours spirit of wine <term>spirit of wine: high-proof alcohol or ethanol used as a solvent.</term>, lets it extract, and separates the pure from the impure <note>original: purum ab impuro</note>. ## CHAPTER VIII.

### Concerning the Sulfur of Vitriol. <note>original: De Sulphure Vitrioli; Vitriol refers to sulfate minerals, most commonly iron or copper sulfate, prized for their medicinal and transformative properties.</note>

->I.<-

From vitriol, a lye is made using beechwood ashes, and from this vitriol, a sulfur is drawn and precipitated with salt of tartar <term>Salt of Tartar: Potassium carbonate, often obtained by burning the tartar—potassium bitartrate—found in wine barrels; used as a precipitating agent.</term>. Furthermore, the oil of sulfur <note>original: Oleum Sulphuris</note> is extracted with oil of juniper <note>original: Oleo juniperi</note>, whereby it becomes a red oil; this same oil is putrefied with spirit of wine <term>spirit of wine: high-proof alcohol or ethanol, used here to refine and stabilize the oil.</term>, and the spirit of wine is then drawn off <note>distilled away</note>. This is a magnificent oil of sulfur to be used in many diseases, such as consumption <note>original: Schwindsucht; tuberculosis</note>, dropsy <note>original: Wassersucht; edema</note>, pestilence, gravel <note>original: Grieß; kidney or bladder stones</note>, and the itch <note>original: Kräze; likely scabies or general skin eruptions</note>.

->2.<-

The vitriol is also sublimated with sal ammoniac <term>Sal ammoniac: Ammonium chloride, a salt used in alchemy to aid the sublimation—turning a solid into vapor and back—of minerals.</term>; this is better than using the lye, because the body of the vitriol <note>original: corpus vitrioli</note> is better dissolved. This sublimate dissolves into oil; with it, one can coagulate and fix <note>to turn a volatile liquid into a stable solid</note> crude mercury <note>original: Mercurium crudum</note>. I will write more about this later when I come to the subject of vitriol.

# CHAPTER III.

<margin>Mars 1</margin>
## On the Vitriol of Iron. <note>original: Vitriolo Martis; Mars is the alchemical name for Iron.</note>

->Recipe.<-

Take Iron filings and Sulfur in equal parts <note>original: ana; a medical term indicating equal quantities of each ingredient</note>, and calcine <term>Calcine: To heat a substance to a high temperature in a furnace or kiln until it is reduced to a dry powder.</term> them in a brick kiln until they turn a purple color; then pour distilled water or vinegar over it, which extracts a beautiful green water. Draw this off by two-thirds <note>original: ad tertias; to boil or evaporate the liquid until only one-third of the original volume remains, concentrating the solution</note>, and let it crystallize <note>original: schiessen; literally "to shoot," referring to the way crystals suddenly form or "shoot" out of a saturated solution</note>. Thus you have an artificial Vitriol <term>Vitriol: Historically, a term for metallic sulfates. Here it refers to iron sulfate crystals.</term>, from which you should distill a red spirit or oil.
Take one Loht <term>Loht: A traditional Germanic unit of weight, roughly equal to 15 grams or half an ounce.</term> of this oil, and add to it a Mercurial Water <note>A powerful solvent or "liquid mercury" preparation capable of dissolving precious metals</note> in which Gold is dissolved (you only need half a Loht of the oil), and fix <term>Fix: To stabilize a volatile substance so that it can withstand high heat without evaporating.</term> this Tincture. Then you have a magnificent medicine to cast upon lead, silver, and tin, and they will be turned into nothing but pure Gold.

O Christian heart, thank the Creator of metals, minerals, and all things.

## SECTION III.
### ON THE COMMON MAGNET.

->1.<-

The magnet possesses within itself that which common Iron <term>Mars: The alchemical and astrological name for Iron.</term> also contains. However, you can easily work with common Iron; therefore, I will refrain from describing its complexities at length. But the lodestone <note>original: *Magnetstein*</note> has an attractive power within it to draw Iron to itself.

->2.<-

An oil is also made from the lodestone and Iron, which performs its duty well in medicine for deep wounds.

->3.<-

With the magnet and Antimony, a "fixed Moon" <term>Luna fixa: Silver that has been rendered stable against heat, often as a precursor to gold.</term> is also made, which is then refined <note>original: *gradirt*; to increase the purity or "grade" of a metal.</note> through the Oil of Iron and Copper <note>original: *Oleum Martis & Veneris*</note> and turned into gold. However, one can also accomplish this with Antimony and Iron.

Thus I have now finished my course and labored, and found much: for my brothers in the Order have all become chemists <note>original: *Chymisten*; practitioners of alchemy.</note> and have all possessed the Philosopher’s Stone <note>original: *Lapidem philosophorum*; the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and healing all illnesses.</note>. I, however, was the beginner and endured great toil before I learned and profited anything. If you will now diligently read my writings, you will from my—

# To make the Salt of the Sun.

Purify gold <note>original: "Solis," symbolized by the Sun</note> three times through antimony, laminate it, and dissolve it in Aqua Regia <note>original: "Aqua Regis," literally "royal water," a powerful mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids used to dissolve noble metals</note>; then dissolve Salt of Tartar <note>original: "Sal Tartari," or potassium carbonate</note> in Spirit of Wine <note>original: "Spiritu Vini," ethanol</note>, draw off the phlegm <note>original: "Phlegma," the watery, tasteless distillate</note> so that it remains like an oil. With this, precipitate the gold and wash the Salt of Tartar from it again. Then calcine <note>original: "reverberirs," to heat in a reverberatory furnace where the flame is reflected onto the material</note> it for fourteen days. Onto this Gold Calx <note>the powdered oxide of gold</note> pour wine vinegar and let it boil gently day and night; thus the vinegar dissolves the Salt from the calcined gold. Whatever remains undissolved at the bottom, calcine that for another eight days. Then boil it again with fresh vinegar and pour it into the other solution; if something still remains, calcine it for another eight days until the "Body" is in the vinegar. Then draw off the vinegar in a water bath <note>original: "Balneo Mariæ," a vessel of hot water used for gentle, even heating</note>; thus you have the Salt of the Sun <note>original: "Sal Solis"</note> in a yellowish powder; it cures all ailments.

### Augmentation <note>original: "Augmentatio," the process of increasing the power or quantity of the alchemical Stone</note>

<margin>3 parts filled</margin>
Take one part of the green dissolving salt-stone <note>likely referring to the purified vitriol or "Lion" mentioned on the previous page</note> and two parts of the tincture before it is added to the gold. Place it in the <term>phial</term> <note>original: "Phiol," a glass vessel</note> according to the amount of material. As soon as it warms up, it will turn black. Return it to the previous degree of heat; it will then become <term>fixed</term> <note>chemically stable and resistant to evaporation by heat</note> again and increased in its quality a thousandfold. This occurs within four weeks, before all the colors cycle through again, and this is an augmentation in quality. The other augmentation occurs when you add it to gold; this is an augmentation in quantity. The more often you restart the tincture in this way, the higher and better its preparation becomes, so that eventually you may increase it in fourteen days—indeed, in a single day or even an hour.

# The Preparation of Basilius Valentinus’s Great Philosopher’s Stone.

In the end and in closing, I will now teach—through the Love of God—how I prepared my **Universal Medicine** <note>original: *Universal-Artzney*; a substance believed to cure all diseases and perfect all metals</note> or **Great Stone of the Wise**, upon which so many builders <note>a common alchemical metaphor for practitioners attempting the Great Work</note> have labored. I will—God be my witness—withhold nothing from you, but rather faithfully and truly reveal all the manual operations <note>original: *Handgriffe*; the specific physical techniques used in the laboratory</note>. Know, then, that this Stone is made out of its own essence; for it transforms other metals into a true **Salt** <note>original: *Saltz*; in alchemy, the "Salt" represents the physical body or the crystalline principle of a substance</note>, which salt must be broken down and once again become a superior Stone. And although nothing foreign must be present in our Stone, the preparation (otherwise called the "breaking") of our Stone cannot initially happen without a medium <note>original: *ohne Mittel*; meaning a catalyst or intermediary substance is required to begin the reaction</note>.

<margin>The margin contains a small hand-drawn triangle containing the letter 'A' <note>This symbol often represents 'Air' in alchemical notation, or may refer to the 'Alpha' or the beginning of the work</note>.</margin>

But take note, as you will hear, that all **corrosives** <note>sharp, acidic substances used to dissolve metals</note> must be washed away <note>original: *abluiret*; from the Latin *abluere*, to wash or cleanse</note> from it again, so that it is separated from all poison and prepared into the highest medicine. I pray this of you, however, by God the Prince of Heaven: that you guard your mouth and press a lock and strong seal upon your lips, so that what you learn from this concerning such unbelievable worldly glory remains kept in silence. It must remain hidden from the unbelieving, the unrepentant, and the unworthy, lest you unnecessarily become a partaker in the sins of others and thereby prepare your own path to hell and damnation; from which may Almighty God faithfully preserve you. Therefore, receive my speech and take my voice to heart; do not think it a slight matter that I [present] the thing simply...

Take one part of the best gold <note>original: *auri optimi*</note> that you can obtain, and six parts of good Hungarian Antimony <note>Antimony, often called the "Grey Wolf," was used by alchemists to purify gold by "devouring" other metallic impurities</note>. Thus it settles into a **Regulus** <note>original: *König* (King); the metallic mass that settles at the bottom of the mold</note>. Refine this Regulus again until it is pure, so that the Antimony is removed from it. When that is done, add new Antimony to it, melt it again, and refine it again. Repeat this for a third time; then the gold is sufficiently purified for the beginning of the work. Afterward, beat the gold thin, as goldsmiths do when they gild, and make an **amalgam** <note>a paste made by mixing a metal with mercury</note> out of it with common mercury. Squeeze this through a leather cloth and let the mercury gradually evaporate <note>original: *abrauchen*</note> over a gentle fire so that nothing more remains of it. Stir it constantly with a small iron hook, and thus the gold becomes "subtle" <note>reduced to an extremely fine, porous powder</note>, so that it can be better attacked and dissolved by its water.

Then take the other part of the **pure mercury of the sun** <term>Mercurius puri solis: the "mercury" or spiritual essence extracted from gold</term> that you have kept, and pour all of this upon it as its own **oil** <term>oleum</term>. Distill it—though not too strongly—**by means of an alembic** <note>original: *per alembicum*; a distillation head or cap</note>. In this way, a little **watery waste** <term>phlegma: the inactive, liquid byproduct of distillation</term> passes over, and the **oil precipitates** <note>original: *oleum præcipitirt*; the solid separates from the liquid solution</note> its own **mercury**, and it becomes white again as the green color is lost. You will find by weight that there are two parts of the **oil of the sun** <term>olei solis: the red "sulfur" or soul of the gold</term> to one part of the **precipitated mercury**. Then place the **mercury** into the glass and add the **oil of the sun** to it. See to it that three parts of the glass remain empty and only the fourth part is filled. **Seal it hermetically** <note>original: *sigilla Hermeticè*; an airtight seal, usually made by melting the glass neck shut</note> and place it in the triple furnace. Let it stand freely inside, no warmer than an egg that is to be hatched by a hen <note>The "hen's heat" is a standard alchemical reference to a gentle, constant warmth, roughly 100°F/38°C</note>. In one month, the matter will enter into **putrefaction** <term>putrefaction: the *Nigredo* or "black stage," representing the death and decomposition of the material before its purification</term> and will become very dark black. When you see this, it is certain that the matter has been unlocked through **putrefaction**; rejoice at the beginning of your good fortune.

Then strengthen the fire to the second degree; in time, the blackness will disappear and change into many wonderful colors <note>This stage is often called the "Peacock's Tail" (*cauda pavonis*)</note>. When these colors have also vanished, strengthen the fire to the third degree, and you will see the glass looking like pure **silver leaf** <note>original: *Silberblech*; this is the *Albedo* or white stage</note>, and the rays will become heavy. Then use the fourth degree of fire, and the mists and vapors will gradually subside. The glass will appear as if it were coated on the inside with pieces of gold. Then continue with a steady fire, and the golden rays will also disappear until finally no more rising of any rays can be seen. Instead, you will see the **matter** <term>Materiam</term> lying at the bottom like a brown **oil**, which finally, when it has become dry, looks like a gray stone, which

### Supplement of Brother Basilius Valentinus.

...which is fixed and constant, also fluid like wax, penetrating like an oil, and of an excellent weight. Whoever attains this, let him thank God his Creator, for poverty has vanished from him, and sickness will flee from him. For this noble medicine is such a stone that nothing in the whole world can be compared to it in virtue, wealth, power, honor, and authority; rather, it is to be preferred above all earthly things, as far as the circumference of the world extends.

Now, when your medicine is finished and you wish to propagate it further for multiplication: Take three parts of the prepared purple-colored gold powder, made as before; add one part of your prepared tincture to it in a new "heaven" <note>A "heaven" refers to a clean, spherical glass vessel used in the final stages of the work.</note>. Seal it hermetically <term>Hermetice: an airtight seal made by melting the glass neck of a vessel shut</term>, place it back in the furnace as before, and the matter <term>Materia: the physical substance undergoing the alchemical process</term> will unite and dissolve <note>original: *solviren*</note> of itself. It will reach its completion in thirty-one days—which is one month—whereas otherwise ten months would have to pass. In this way, you can multiply your medicine without end, so that such things can be accomplished as the whole world is unable to believe. May the highest God and Creator be highly praised for eternity for this unspeakable benefit, as well as for all his fatherly gifts and bestowed wisdom. Amen.

Finally, however, you should know that this medicine is very spiritual and penetrating; it takes away all infirmities of this world, whatever they may be, in all creatures. If a single grain <term>Gran: a tiny unit of measurement, approximately 0.06 grams</term> is used, it permeates the entire body like a smoke, gnaws away everything evil, establishes something better in its place, cleanses the human being, and makes of him as if a new birth. Thus, it preserves him without any accident <note>In this context, "accident" refers to external ailments, symptoms, or the ravages of disease.</note> until a ripe old age and until the goal set for him by the Most High. Also, this medicine—having first been fermented <term>fermentiret: the process of "fixing" the spiritual stone with physical gold to stabilize its power</term> with other fine gold—tinges <note>original: *tingiret*; to "tinge" or dye the internal nature of a metal, effectively transforming it</note> many thousand parts of all other metals into the best gold, just as my final Twelfth Key teaches through a certain way and process.

By this means, such gold becomes a penetrating medicine, of which one part will further tinge and transmute <term>transmutiren: the fundamental alchemical change of one element into another</term> a thousand parts of other metals—and even unbelievably more—into true gold. God be praised for eternity. Amen.

above the Rhine, and thus presumably in Alsace. He was most famous—indeed even at the Imperial and other great courts—in the fourteenth century <note>original: "vierzehenden Seculo"; historical evidence suggests the writings attributed to Valentinus actually appeared later, in the 1600s</note> after Christ's birth, and primarily toward the end of that century.
